body:
WARRANT#173 shipped: the CERBERUS gate skeleton (Part IX), all 8 gates -- G-REACH, G-POWER, G-STALE, G-STACK, G-SEED, G-TELE, G-SELF, G-COST. Real logic, not stubs.

Each gate's self-test reproduces a REAL incident from this project as its known-answer case -- G-POWER's test IS the Aug-6 ghostWR-100%-n=1 read, G-STALE's test IS the WARRANT#72 37-day staleness, G-TELE's test IS the SentinelRecordOutcome shape. Ran the self-tests before trusting any of it (the module's own G-SELF rule, applied to itself) and it caught 3 real bugs on the first run -- including one that would have made G-TELE blind to plain global variables like g_SentinelMult (no dot in the name), which is literally the exact incident that gate exists to catch. Fixed, re-ran, all 8 pass now.

Then validated G-SEED against the REAL current TUNGSTEN source, not just synthetic tests: it correctly reports g_Risk.minRisk now has 2 real assignment sites and is not flagged -- matching WARRANT#167's actual fix from earlier tonight. That's the tool checking its answer against ground truth we already know, not just internal consistency.

Honestly incomplete, named not hidden: G-SELF is a registry a person/agent consults, it doesn't yet automatically block anything. G-COST correctly can't produce a number -- there are no live fills. Part IX.2's automatic trial-count reading from forge_ledger.json isn't wired yet.

State of the ship order now: steps 1 (path-state), 2 (export bridge) shipped in MQL4; the research-layer scaffold and now the CERBERUS gate skeleton both built and self-tested in parallel. Everything genuinely buildable ahead of real trade data is now built. What's left needs either real closed trades (none yet -- market hasn't opened on tonight's build) or a decision on the Python dependency situation (purgedcv, for DSR/PBO/CPCV). I'm not going to manufacture progress past that -- that's exactly what the document itself says not to do.
